bio: Nino enjoys iPad, videogames (especially Minecraft), social outings, movies, eating out, trampoline, bowling, swimming, Scienceworks, dinosaur exhibits, Greek food, music, coffee, and camps. He is a Minecraft fan — his visual support boards use Minecraft themes. He is good with names and faces. Likes: pizza, Greek food, cake, toast, banana, apple, plain rice, schnitzel, chips, pasta, KFC. Dislikes chewy foods. Loves music videos and YouTube for self-regulation. Community access (bowling, drives, shopping, movies, coffee outings) keeps him well-regulated and in positive mood. Transitioning from Aruma to One Life Foundation.
gp_clinic: Alphington Medical Centre, 29-31 Station St, Fairfield VIC 3078
notes:
KEY HEALTH ALERT: Epilepsy (Idiopathic Generalised) — Midazolam 10mg buccal if tonic-clonic seizure >5 mins, call 000 immediately. Seizure types: (1) Generalised Tonic-Clonic — full body convulsion, 2-5 min, occurred 4 times lifetime; (2) Unresponsive staring episodes — up to 5 min. No known triggers but illness/poor sleep increase risk. Pre-seizure signs: glazed/glaring, unusually docile. Post-seizure: confused/drowsy, may repeat sounds for comfort, recovery 30-60 min. Showers only (no baths), cold tap first, hot tap off first.

KEY SAFETY: Must be in workers line of sight at all times (has tracker in bag). Do not get into his space or force him — respect "No". May bite if anxious/frustrated.

BEHAVIOUR SUMMARY: Primary behaviour of concern is hand/thumb biting. Triggers: internet/TV not working, non-preferred tasks, routine changes, activity delays, communication difficulties, being asked to stop watching TV/YouTube. Strong reliance on routine and predictability. Prompt-dependent for daily tasks (morning routines, showering, personal care, household tasks). Initial refusal/delay ("5 more minutes") then eventual compliance with encouragement. Generally calm and settled — very few significant escalations.

ESCALATION SIGNS: Squinted eyes, lowered head, restless pacing, hand flapping, throat vocalisations, repeating statements, jumping while flapping, pushing hands away, becoming silent/withdrawn, covering ears, feigned crying.

DE-ESCALATION: Give 15-30 min warnings before transitions. Offer 2 choices at a time. Use visual boards (Who Is Supporting Me + Daily Plan — Minecraft themed). Acknowledge calmly at first signs. Offer star jumps/hand squeezes/shoulder rubs. Prompt "Use your words". Break tension with humour or Madagascar movie quotes. Keep voice low and neutral during escalation. Do not turn back when heightened. Do not sit down — remain standing. Use natural barriers for protection. If behaviours escalate beyond 15 min: administer PRN as prescribed.

DAILY STRUCTURE: Use Who Is Supporting Me board (AM/PM/Night staff names). Use Daily Plan board (offer 2 activity choices, cross off completed). Monday meal planning with weekly meal board. Prioritise community outings and movement activities in afternoon (gym, swimming, boxing, trampoline). Avoid unstructured days and extended passive screen time (>1 hour — redirect).

PERSONAL CARE: Needs assistance with showering (water temp regulation, prompting to wash body/hair), hair washing, shaving (electric), oral hygiene. Independent with toileting, dressing, grooming.

SLEEP: Usually settles 10-11pm, watches TV/YouTube before sleep. Melatonin at bedtime. Slow to wake, needs multiple prompts. Regular daytime fatigue/napping. Fatigue increases later in day.

communication_needs: Limited verbal communication — uses single words (e.g. "Coke"), needs encouragement for full sentences. Does not initiate social interaction but is good with names/faces. May ask for a hug if upset. Needs simple, calm verbal requests. Currently transitioning to a new communication device (speech pathology ongoing). Receptive language: does NOT readily comprehend without adjusted language. Can notify others of pain (will be very quiet and ask for hugs, or tell you).
mobility: Independent mobility, no aids required. No vision issues, no balance issues, no falls risk. Fearless (per mother) — supervision needed near heights, roads. Helmet required for bike/scooter.
dietary_requirements: SWALLOWING RISK — has nearly choked twice in 18 months (back blows required). Must cut food into smaller pieces, one bite at a time, chew food 16 times, swallow before drinking. Speech therapist engaged for swallowing assessment. Use Mealtime Checklist at dining table. Likes: pizza, Greek food, cake, toast, banana, apple, plain rice, schnitzel, chips, pasta. Dislikes: foods too chewy. Prefers not too noisy environment during meals.
allergies: No known drug or food allergies
medications_summary: REGULAR: Epilim (Sodium Valproate) 100mg + 500mg twice daily (epilepsy); Intuniv (Guanfacine) 4mg once daily after dinner (ADHD); Risperidone 0.5mg — AM 1 tab, PM 2 tabs + PRN for agitation (behavioural); Melatonin 2mg SR (Circadin) once at bedtime (sleep). PRN: Risperidone 0.5mg extra for meltdowns; Midazolam 10mg BUCCAL if seizure >5 minutes then call 000; Paracetamol 500mg 1-2 tabs 4-6 hourly max 8/day; Ibuprofen 200mg 1-2 tabs; Bromhexine 8mg 1 tab 3x/day for chesty cough; Movicol 1 sachet for constipation; Promethazine 25mg for sleep (PRN). Full assistance required for all medication administration. Meds stored in bag or Quick St staff room locked cupboard. Weight: 100kg.
